transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
- Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Dave Mattingly.
Wall Street is coming off its sharpest day of gains
in more than a year and a half.
It was sparked by computer chip giant Nvidia
announcing its board was reinstating Jensen Huang
as the company's president and CEO effective immediately.
The unanimous vote by the board came less than two weeks
after Huang resigned, having acknowledged an affair
with a woman reported to be a Chinese spy.
NPR's Katie McHugh says Huang is scheduled
to testify to several congressional committees next week.
- Huang is scheduled to face the foreign affairs
and intelligence committees and also the select committee
on the Chinese Communist Party.
Those sessions will take place behind closed doors.
Lawmakers are demanding answers
about Nvidia's alleged role in chip smuggling
and evading U.S. export controls designed
to keep advanced AI chips out of China.
They'll also seek more information
about Huang's affair with a woman
who U.S. officials say is linked
to China's top spy agency.
The Committee on Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs
has announced it will meet with Huang,
which will be open and broadcast as a live webcast.
Katie McHugh, NPR News, New York.
- The Dow gained 3% yesterday.
The S&P 500 added more than 4.5%.
The tech-heavy NASDAQ finished up 6.5%.
The Democrats' next presidential debate schedule
is taking shape.
Here's NPR's Tamara Keefe.
- The Democratic National Committee has announced
its 2028 presidential debate schedule.
A dozen debates with as many as 20 candidates
allowed to qualify.
The first one is set for next June.
The Republican Party debate schedule
won't be announced until early next year
after a contested election
for chair of the Republican National Committee.
- That's NPR's Tamara Keefe reporting.
Poland is asking NATO to bolster its share
of the country's air defenses in response to Russia
firing several missiles into Polish territory.
That happened late last week as European forces
were carrying out military exercises
about 30 to 60 miles away.
Terry Schulz says more from Brussels.
- After NATO ambassadors held an emergency meeting
at Poland's request,
the alliance's top military commander, Alexis Grinkowicz,
told Poland he would deploy one of the alliance's
shared AWACS aircraft to help the country
better defend itself against errant Russian missiles.
NATO spokesperson, Alison Hart, says Grinkowicz
is also looking at what other assets may be sent to Poland
after three Russian ballistic missiles landed
in the eastern part of the country Friday
without being intercepted.
Polish Deputy Defense Minister, Pavel Zilevski,
says the AWACS plane, one of 14 NATO has based in Germany,
will give Poland better operational awareness
to respond to this kind of threat.
For NPR News, I'm Terry Schultz in Brussels.
- Wall Street Futures are on the downside this morning.
Dow Futures are off about 12 points.
This is NPR News from Washington.
Soccer's world governing body, FIFA,
says the 2031 Women's World Cup
will be co-hosted by the U.S.
The other host countries are Mexico,
Jamaica, and Costa Rica.
In addition, FIFA says the tournament
will mark the first time 48 teams will compete.
Next year's Women's World Cup soccer tournament
is being hosted by Brazil.
Brazil's former president remains hospitalized.
Jair Bolsonaro was admitted late last week
as he was transferred from house arrest.
Bolsonaro has been serving a lengthy prison sentence
stemming from a failed coup, as Julia Carnero reports.
- Jair Bolsonaro was diagnosed
with acute bowel obstruction and pneumonia
and remains under intensive care
at a private hospital in Brasilia.
According to the latest medical report,
he is clinically stable,
but there is no scheduled date for his discharge,
and further surgery remains a possibility
if his condition deteriorates.
His bowel condition is linked to the stab
he suffered in 2018 in a campaign rally
before being elected president,
which has led to several surgeries.
This week marks a year since Bolsonaro
started his 27-year sentence
for attempting a coup to stay in power
after losing re-elections.
Since March, he has been under house arrest
due to his health conditions.
For NPR News, I'm Julia Carnero in Rio.
- The National Weather Service
says areas of the West Coast
could see coastal flooding this week.
Advisories and warnings are in effect
in coastal areas of California,
as well as Oregon and Washington.
Forecasters say a series of Pacific storms
will bring widespread rain and gusty winds.
I'm Dave Mattingly in Washington.

topics.text: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after affair with alleged Chinese spy
Huang to testify behind closed doors before congressional committees next week
Dow, S&P 500, and NASDAQ post sharp gains following Nvidia news
DNC releases 2028 presidential debate schedule, first debate set for June
Poland requests NATO help after Russian ballistic missiles land in its territory
NATO commander deploys AWACS aircraft to bolster Poland's air defenses
FIFA names U.S., Mexico, Jamaica, Costa Rica co-hosts of 2031 Women's World Cup
Former Brazilian president Bolsonaro hospitalized in Brasilia with bowel obstruction and pneumonia
National Weather Service issues coastal flood advisories along West Coast this week
